queries: WITH pat AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) AS alb, AVG(1.0 * l.UN / NULLIF(l."T-BIL", 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sx AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM pat GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM sx) SELECT sx.SEX, sx.avg_alb, sx.avg_ratio, sx.avg_alb - m.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM sx CROSS JOIN m WHERE sx.avg_alb > m.mean_alb

WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(L.ALB) AS alb, AVG(CAST(L.UN AS REAL) / NULLIF(L.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(P.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM s) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_ratio, s.avg_alb - m.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE s.avg_alb > m.mean_alb

WITH patient_level AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) AS alb, AVG(1.0 * l.UN / NULLIF(l.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sex_level AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_un_tbil_ratio FROM patient_level GROUP BY SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM sex_level) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_un_tbil_ratio, s.avg_alb - o.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM sex_level s CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE s.avg_alb > o.mean_alb ORDER BY s.SEX

assumptions.assumption: The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages (each sex counts once), not a mean over all patients or lab rows.
The UN/T-BIL ratio is computed per lab row, and rows with T-BIL of 0 or NULL give no ratio and are ignored. Each patient's ratio is the average of their row ratios.
Blank SEX means an empty or whitespace-only string. These patients and NULL-SEX patients are excluded before the mean is computed.

assumptions.assumption: The ratio UN/T-BIL is computed per lab record and then averaged per patient. A T-BIL of 0 gives a NULL ratio, which the averages ignore.
The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages, with each sex counting once.
A blank SEX means an empty or whitespace-only string. These patients and those with NULL SEX are excluded.

assumptions.assumption: The UN to T-BIL ratio is computed for each lab record (each test row) and then averaged within a patient. Records with T-BIL of 0 or NULL, or UN NULL, give a NULL ratio and are ignored.
The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted mean across the sexes that remain after the blank/missing SEX filter. It is not weighted by patient count.
A blank SEX means an empty or whitespace-only string.
